customer: Hi, so I'm hoping someone can help me sort this out, because between the baby waking up every two hours and everything else I've kind of lost track of the paperwork side of things. We paid off the loan on our minivan a while back and I was thinking about selling it to you, but when I dug out the title the bank is still listed on it as the lienholder, which I thought would have gone away once it was paid. I'm in Texas if that matters at all. Is this going to hold everything up, and what do I actually need to do?
agent: Congratulations on the new baby, and thanks for reaching out! As our article "My loan is paid off but the lien is still on the title" explains, this means the lien hasn't been released yet, so the first step is to ask your lender for a lien release letter. If you can't get one, you can sign our lien release request, form NW-LRL-1, and we'll contact the lender for you, though this can add 1 to 2 weeks. Either way, we can still make an offer on your minivan and book your appointment while you wait, and in states with electronic titles the lender sends the release to the state electronically.
